Nordel is an MLS® sub-area in North Delta, in the City of Delta. On the MLS® map it takes in the area west of about 112 Street, with homes on streets such as Wiltshire Boulevard, Brooke Road, Norum Road and River Road. Burns Bog and the Delta Nature Reserve are on its west side.
are next door to the east. The City’s Nordel Social Heart, around 84 Avenue and 112 Street, is its planned community centre.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 15, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Delta and Delta School District.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

parts.t: Zoning and plan designations can be different for each lot.
Delta Council adopted the Official Community Plan 2024, “Housing Our Future” (Bylaw No. 8400), on July 8, 2024.

The OCP has a Nordel Social Heart development permit area (ND12). Its goal is to revitalize Nordel as a node of shops, recreation, culture and education, with a mix of homes including multi-family, as the community focus for North Delta.

The OCP says the focus for growth in North Delta includes the Nordel Social Heart and the 84 Avenue corridor. It describes a commercial node at 112 Street and 84 Avenue that serves the surrounding neighbourhoods.
The North Delta Area Plan (revised March 2015) also calls the area near 84 Avenue and 112 Street the “Social Heart” of North Delta. It allows a moderate amount of added residential density there.

Delta changed its zoning in 2024 so that many single detached and duplex lots can have a secondary suite plus up to two detached suites (a garden suite or coach house). The rules differ by lot, so ask me or the City about an address.
From MLS® sales data (not an official source): the median lot size of detached houses sold from July 1 to October 8, 2026 was 7,238 square feet, across 26 sales with a recorded lot size.
Check the land near Burns Bog.
Burns Bog is protected, and the City monitors and works to improve the bog’s water levels (its hydrology).
If a home is close to the bog, ask the City about drainage and the exact lot.
Check the river bank and any slope.

The OCP says the Fraser River waterfront, river bank and ravine slopes in its Fraser River Escarpment area (ND1) are subject to erosion and land slip. If a home is near the river or a slope, ask the City about the exact lot.
Ask the City what the plans allow on the lots around the home, especially near 84 Avenue and 112 Street.
